critical_paths.property: M6 requires the liquid reserve to cover admitted restoration work after any creator-authorized close and reopen sequence.
critical_paths.attacker_control: Creator can close, claim the full closed-state surplus and reopen while all Shape prizes remain listed.
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: Liquid ETH leaves Balancer for creator, Shape backing stays in live tokens at Shapes, player payment enters FWA escrow.
critical_paths.counterexample: The pinned fork admitted a real player draw with Balancer liquid balance zero against a 100.034 ETH reserve requirement.

postconditions.assertion: After reopening, the pool has zero liquid ETH but admits a real FWA purchase.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: A direct admissionStatus read could pass without the real FWA nested purchase hook executing.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: Fund an external player and execute the real FWA acquire path after close, drain and reopen.

critical_paths.property: M6 requires the pre-burst liquid reserve plus proceeds to restore the target after all admitted outcomes.
critical_paths.attacker_control: Creator claims all permitted surplus and a player issues two FWA draws; VRF outcomes are a reachability witness only.
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: After the maximum permitted claim and two real coordinator-delivered wins, the Balancer holds 0.474750884357087310 ETH against 1.035 ETH required reserve; the cited strict-route test does not separately assert exact owner proceeds.
critical_paths.counterexample: Two coordinator→service-delivered prizes of 0.5 and 0.1 ETH leave the 0.5 ETH prize absent; another upkeep cannot mint it and a third FWA purchase succeeds.

postconditions.assertion: After one upkeep, the 0.1 ETH target is restored, the 0.5 ETH target remains absent, admission is zero, and a third real FWA purchase succeeds after the two-win burst.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: A direct pool callback can bypass router reservations, an inline getter can consume a payer prank, and a second no-progress upkeep was not asserted in the cited strict-route test.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: Deliver words as the actual coordinator through the real VRF service, pre-read FWA inventory version, assert EOA payer balance deltas, then buy again.

critical_paths.property: A funded player who draws a curated NFT receives actual transferable ownership or the failed-delivery acquisition-fee refund; creator cannot repeatedly sell one token while retaining it.
critical_paths.attacker_control: Creator chooses a deliberately dishonest ERC721 collection whose transferFrom and ownerOf fabricate escrow and delivery. Coordinator words are supplied only to show reachable selections, not creator control.
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: Players each lose 0.025199431673280128 ETH; FWA sends owner proceeds of 0.021659458736457265 ETH per selected sale to Balancer; creator reclaims 1.040970886022914530 ETH after 1 ETH funding while internal ERC721 owner never changes.
critical_paths.counterexample: FWA marks both sales fulfilled/delivered and rejects both refunds despite internal token ownership staying at creator; one ghost NFT is sold twice.

postconditions.assertion: Two funded EOA draws are FWA status2/listing4 after coordinator→service words, both refunds reject after seven days, internal ERC721 owner remains creator, and final creator net is +0.040970886022914530 ETH excluding gas.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: A collection ownerOf return may lie, a test-contract payer may replace the named EOA, or direct pool callback may bypass router accounting.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: Use the hostile collection internal owner ledger, pre-read inventory versions, assert both EOA balance decreases and actual coordinator→service callbacks, then attempt both refunds and closeout.
